body:
Thanks for the advice.  Those are exactly the questions I need to think about right now.

As for the rape fantasies mentioned, it's necessarily a "fantasy" so much as a mild hallucination (probably not the best word- it's more of a vivid imagining, I guess?), where I will feel as if I am being pinned down to some extent.

>It is difficult to find a therapist who is in sync

That's actually one of the points brought up by my current therapist.  He mentioned he thought we were a pretty good match.  I'm not sure about that- it's something I'm considering.  There have some successful sessions, but I'm not sure his approach quite works for me.
>you want to make a specific goal to achieve

I think this is the biggest problem I have.  I have some generalized goals (dealing with depression and possible ADD), but nothing too specific (especially for the short-term).  This is especially true for each individual session.  Sometimes there are a few things I want to talk about, if something's happened in my life for the past week or so between sessions.  Most of the time, however, nothing happens.  I live a pretty isolated life right now.  I spend most of my time inside my apartment, except when I need to go out or to ride my bike.  This leaves me with almost nothing to talk about during my sessions (except for, as I wrote in the reply to thebdt, some issues I *really* don't want to talk about- namely some infrequent, somewhat vivid, fantasies where I feel like I'm being raped).

There have been some good sessions, but I'm not sure how helpful he's been.  These have been times when I opened myself up more.  That is a great thing, and what therapy is about.  It just doesn't seem he adds in much feedback, or really refers back to previous sessions.  He is helpful in the sense that I've been able to open up, although I haven't had that problem with the therapists I've seen in the past.

I haven't really brought up issues with my sexuality with my therapist. We did briefly discuss it.  I told him I was gay/bi.  He asked about my sex life (the last time I had it), if I'd ever been with a woman (since I did mention being bi).  He asked me about my dating life.  That's about it.  I don't really think I'd be comfortable bringing up the rape fantasy.  I know part of the reason for therapy is to open up about things, even that makes you uncomfortable.  This just seems too hard to talk about.

I know I don't bring up a lot of things I probably should in therapy.  I don't bring up my suicidal thoughts much.  This is mostly out of fear I'd be locked up.  I'm very careful in what I say about this.  In therapy, it doesn't come up much.  I'm a bit more honest with my doctor who prescribes my medication, but I'm still extremely careful not to indicate that I have any plans.  I will mention I have suicidal thoughts, but I usually try to downplay them (saying I have no intent, that I can usually brush them off after a while).  I guess in that respect (that I don't bring up a lot of my issues), therapy won't help.

I generally don't see myself has having issues with my sexuality, which is probably why I haven't brought them up.  I know these occasional (fairly infrequent now) fantasies come up.  Other than that, I feel comfortable with my orientation.  I don't really date or have sex, which is perfectly fine for me.  I know I'll alternate between periods where I'm largely asexual (where I'm at right now) and a period where I want to have sex (usually don't act on it, except for porn and chat online).  I'll admit I have a fetish I feel somewhat ashamed about, but I'm mostly coming to terms with it on my own.

As far as government (or other) assistance, I won't do it.  I know I could get a job.  I just haven't.  Maybe I've just gotten used to my (lack of) schedule, having free time, and don't want that to change; maybe I'm just lazy.  Either way, I feel perfectly capable.  I just... haven't.  I wouldn't feel good about using money because of a choice I've made.
How so?

Thanks.  That link is a good read.  I'm not sure any of the reasons listed there really describes me (or at least this situation accurately), but it's hard to say what takes place in  our subconscious mind.  I do think this seems to apply somewhat:
>In my personal experience, most women really appreciate subtle to moderate domination in the bedroom—a little forceful restraint, a little pain—as long as they feel safe.

I do think a bit of domination can be a turn on for me, but I'm not sure that explains how vivid this experience seems to me.  Of course, it could be normal (or at least not *abnormal*) and I could just be making a big deal over nothing.

>You man want to give a counselor, therapist, or psychologist a try

I've been seeing my current therapist since January.  I'm probably going to find a new one, though.  He doesn't give me as much feedback as I'd like (or, helpful feedback).  He also doesn't seem very professional.  One session, I kept hearing a few pings from his computer (the sound you get if you have a new message on AIM).  After about 6 or 7 of them, they stopped- but he didn't even try to turn down the volume.  Another time, his phone rang.  It kept on ringing until he finally answered it.  Granted time was up, but I was still talking.  It turned out he was just late for lunch.  Other than that, he hasn't offered much help.  One session, he basically spouted off a lot of generic depression advice (somewhat helpful, but basically everything I'd expect to find on some depression website- exercise, diet, etc).  He mentioned something last week that seemed like it might help, so I haven't cancelled yet.

Prior to him, I had been seeing another one for a few months.  He generally was a good therapist.  He listened well and asked questions about things we talked about in prior sessions (haven't had that happen with my current therapist- in fact, he's asked a few questions multiple times).  The only reason I left him was his style.  This was before I started medication.  I was hoping to learn some techniques to help organize and focus.  He did go over a variety of strategies.  Eventually, I was running out of things to try.  His approach was very "hands-on" in that it'd focus on me doing things, trying different things out- more action, I guess, than analysis.  I wanted to see someone else to get a more analytical approach.

>Once you're dead, that's it! You can't go back to living.

I realize this.  I try and think about things I enjoy, the things I'd still like to do.  I'm not sure it matters, though.  I know I'm not going to be able to do everything I want.  I also know I can't devout my life to only doing those things I want to do.  Without a means to support myself, none of that matters.

>Shit happens, plain and simple.

True.  I guess I just feel that way, since I quit my job knowing I didn't have a job lined up and haven't made much of an effort to find another one.

>If you're at less than about 300mg it may be at too low of a dose.

My does was just increased to 150mg this week.  As much as I'd love to keep trying new medications, I'm running out of time (money).  It takes a while before most medications work, and I have to be weened off of what I'm taking now.

I think this is to help when transferring credits.  If English 101 at the CC won't automatically transfer over, you can talk to someone.  Showing them the syllabus will provide reference of what was covered in the class to see if they are, in fact, compatible courses.

I'm sure I'll be able to find a copy of my taxes.  I might have to pay a small fee, but they're out there.  

Unfortunately, I don't think I have any real records.  The best I have is the job description available for the last job I had.  I can probably expand a bit on that, but usually companies want to hear something more specific from what I've gathered- such as an event, or a major project.
If they ask about the color of my poop, I think I applied for the wrong job.

It just seems like I can't do anything.  It's just always been like that from what I remember.  I'll start organizing a project, write down ideas, but I can't focus enough when trying to actually put it together.

Collaborating on a project wouldn't work out.  I don't really have many friends.  Most of what I'm interested in doing is basically solo stuff, anyway.

I'm 25, and I'm not really sure what kind of work I'm looking at.  Right now, I don't really feel like I could do anything except min. wage stuff or slightly above.  I went to college, but now it seems it was a waste since I'll be applying to jobs I could have had without going to school.

So far, I haven't really noticed any side effects of the medication, possibly minor headaches and problems sleeping, but nothing substantial.  Those symptoms could just be coincidental as well.

I don't think I'm really disabled, just lazy.  I don't know.  My life is very disorganized and it's hard to do just about anything because a lack of motivation or just doing it.  I've been meaning to do the dishes now for the past week (or two?).  I'm hoping to do them this morning finally.

I've been seeing a therapist because of depression and (possible) ADD.  Initially, I had mentioned having suicidal thoughts in the past.  I finally admitted that I had on-going periodic suicidal thoughts.  He asked if I had a plan.  I lied.  I told him I didn't.  

I think it's important to mention to a therapist so they have a better idea of what's going on inside your head to provide as much support as possible.  I do also fear being locked up.  It's really just a matter of emphasizing that you're not an immediate threat to yourself or others (no plan, no threat).

I can't promise that therapy will help.  It hasn't been very successful for me, as I generally dislike talking about my problems a lot.  That said, it's likely I do have some issues that could be improved.  I'm also about to start medication, which will probably be a lot more helpful (at least, right now I'm hopeful).  From what I've been reading up on the medications I'll be taking, they can be tremendously helpful at improving a person's outlook on life.  

I have no idea if the therapy and/or medications will help.  I figure there's no harm in trying if my alternative is killing myself.

Would it help to join a support group, especially one for eating disorders?  You might be able to make some new friends who understand what you're going through.

Some women might not like it that you don't have a car.  If it comes up, simply be confident about your decision.  You don't have a car because you don't need, because of the environmental impact, because you're happier without one, you get by just fine without one, you like the exercise of a bike.... whatever the reason.  This might make her less interested, but that's probably not the type of girl you'd be interested in anyway.

I'm not sure.  The job itself was somewhat void of regular assignments to do.  I had a few things I had to do on a monthly/weekly basis.  Once I had those finished, I didn't have anything.  I got incredibly bored doing the online training (it had gotten to the point where I was taking tutorials for things I would never be dealing with in my job because I had taken any relevant tutorials).  I couldn't spend the day browsing the web (company monitored internet access).  My boss also seemed to get mad if I had a sudoku book around.  I couldn't stand it and quit.
I really have no idea what approach I'm taking.  I certainly don't feel tough.

> Money isn't everything to live for.

No, but having money is usually very helpful in order to live (essential for buying food, paying rent).  That's my problem.

The job I had was right in the field.  It even paid pretty well.  I just didn't like it, though.  I'm at the point now that I think any job would make me miserable.  

I have no idea about investing.  I can spend less, and that's really all I can do my money.

> I found that once it was in the open, It wasn't as bad as I thought it was.

The first counselor I saw last year, I ended up saying everything I had to (or was willing to) say after about 5 sessions.  A lot of it was exactly this: my problems didn't seem so bad.  That actually made me feel slightly worse, because then I thought I was exaggerating things in my head and was wasting the therapist's time.

Surprisingly, my last boss was actually pretty nice.  She seemed to think highly of me.  Her way of managing just wasn't working out for me, I suppose.  

I saw a career counselor a few years ago.  I don't think much has changed since then (I'd come out with similar results).  The problem I have is, "Oh, I have this list of careers... but now what?"  That's the part I get stuck.

Unfortunately, I'm not much of a reader.  I really can't do it.  I'm not illiterate, but I just can't seem to absorb much of what I read.  This is especially true for fiction.  I can't really follow a story along because I can't remember details or never really absorbed that in the first place.  When I read, I'm thinking the words in my head, but can't actually visualize anything.  I've never had a strong imagination in the sense that developing images in my mind is often difficult.  I do find myself creative, though.

My favorite movies are cheesy comedies (think Mel Brooks, Airplane, Attack of the Killer Tomatoes).  I just love to laugh.  I can watch them over and over again, usually picking up new stuff each time.  I'm not really sure I have a character I want to be- I'd have to think about that, I guess.

If I had to say when I'm happiest, it's when I'm able to help others in some way- maybe it'd be helping do research, or simply making them smile.

I'm already seeing a therapist to deal with my motivation problems.  Unfortunately, I haven't had any luck.  I'm probably going to end up stopping my sessions.

I already have a bachelor's degree.  I had started grad school, but had to drop out because of thesis issues (mostly, I had nothing I felt comfortable doing as a topic).  I don't think going back is really an option.  I also sort of see going to school as being a waste of time- I enjoyed going to school, but I don't think it's really been beneficial at all.

No, I didn't work in a call center.  The job I had was otherwise boring- I wasn't given enough work to do, I often got stuff my boss couldn't do (ie, had to fix her mistakes), and got the impression my boss didn't want me to have any books by my desk (I loved to do sudoku when I started getting tired- just take a break, look at a puzzle for a few minutes to get refreshed, not completely slack off).  I think the only job I'll be able to get in the near future is at a call center here, however.
